definitions.explanation: A small-scale model or miniature version of something, used as a reference or sample.
A pre-made format or standard document used as a starting point. Common in business and administrative contexts for contracts, letters, and other documents.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{雛形|ひながた}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a model of the castle.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}の{雛形|ひながた}は{博物館|はくぶつかん}に{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: A miniature model of this building is displayed in the museum.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{町|まち}の{雛形|ひながた}が{精巧|せいこう}に{再現|さいげん}されていて、{見|み}ごたえがあった。
examples.english: A miniature of an Edo-period town was recreated in exquisite detail, and it was well worth seeing.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}の{雛形|ひながた}をください。
examples.english: Please give me a template for the contract.

examples.japanese: この{雛形|ひながた}を{参考|さんこう}にして{書類|しょるい}を{作成|さくせい}してください。
examples.english: Please use this template as a reference when preparing the documents.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}では{報告書|ほうこくしょ}の{雛形|ひながた}が{用意|ようい}されているので、{新人|しんじん}でもすぐに{書|か}ける。
examples.english: The company provides report templates, so even new employees can write them right away.

notes:
Originally from {雛|ひな} (chick; miniature) + {形|かた} (shape), suggesting a small copy of the real thing.

SENSE 1 (model):
Refers to physical miniatures or scale models. This is the older, more traditional meaning.

SENSE 2 (template):
The dominant modern usage, especially in business. Refers to standardized document formats.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {契約書|けいやくしょ}の{雛形|ひながた} (contract template)
- {報告書|ほうこくしょ}の{雛形|ひながた} (report template)
- {雛形|ひながた}を{作|つく}る (create a template/model)

SIMILAR WORDS:
テンプレート is the loanword equivalent for sense 2 and is increasingly common, especially in IT contexts. {見本|みほん} (sample) overlaps with sense 1 but emphasizes something shown as an example rather than a scaled-down replica.
